## Internal pull-ups

Many microcontrollers can enable a resistor inside the device. With Arduino-style APIs, `INPUT_PULLUP` enables that resistor. A switch connects the pin to ground, so released reads `HIGH` and pressed reads `LOW`.

```cpp
pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP);
bool pressed = digitalRead(buttonPin) == LOW;
```

Use an external resistor when the internal value is too weak or uncertain, the wire is long or noisy, the input needs a defined reset state, the voltage domain differs, or an RC time constant requires a specific resistance.

## Contact bounce

Mechanical contacts can produce several rapid transitions during one press. Debounce with a timed software state machine, an RC network connected to a suitable threshold input, or a dedicated circuit.

$$\tau=RC$$

![An RC pull-up network filters rapid transitions before the GPIO input.](/assets/tej/RC_Debounce_Input.svg){fig-alt="A pull-up resistor and capacitor connect to the switch and GPIO node to form an RC debounce circuit." width=88%}

## Protection and compatibility

A series resistor and clamp network can limit abnormal current, but it does not turn every 5 V signal into a safe 3.3 V input. Check thresholds, absolute maximum ratings, clamp-current limits, power sequencing, wiring length, and the signal source.

::: {.callout-warning title="3.3 V and 5 V warning"}
Do not imply that all GPIO pins are 5 V tolerant. Confirm the exact board, processor, shield, and sensor before connection.
:::
